scope: Native identity-digest admission for semantic operations and occurrences: byte-exact Rust port of identityDigest/stableJson and of the opv1:/ambv1:/occv1:/entity:v2: derivers, strict validateOperations and the validateOccurrences identity subset behind the WASM ABI
coverage: identityDigest ported byte-exact: SHA-256 (sha2 crate) over big-endian length-prefixed UTF-8 domain plus canonical payload bytes

stableJson ported byte-exact: object keys sorted by raw UTF-8 bytes (BTreeMap order), JSON.stringify string escaping, ECMAScript Number::toString number formatting replicated from the shortest round-trip digits (integer form up to 1e21, 0.000001 boundary, 1e-7 exponential boundary, subnormals, 19 pinned number cases match node String(n) exactly)

All four derivers ported: opv1: operation IDs, ambv1: ambiguity groups, occv1: occurrence IDs over parentId/staticParentId/operationId/dynamicSlots, entity:v2: scene entity IDs; every digest pinned against values produced by running the TS derivers in node, including non-ASCII path names and number/boolean/string/undefined/null/vector dynamic slots

Operations admitted natively: positional IDs, deterministic parent-before-child preorder with stack discipline, exact-once structural path extension, re-derived operation IDs, unique paths and IDs, dense-from-zero sibling child ordinals, ambiguity-group membership iff more than one same-name sibling with a re-derived group ID, identityEvidence consistency

Occurrence identity subset admitted natively: positional IDs, parent/staticParent bounded below the row and targeting the canonical first row of the referenced occurrence ID, staticParent null-ness and static operation instantiation consistency, re-derived occurrence IDs, rows sharing an ID describing the same logical evaluation (operation, parents, dynamic slots), per-ID output rows dense from zero with re-derived scene entity IDs, unique scene entity IDs, dynamic slot duplicate-ordinal density and distinctness

Unknown digest prefixes (opv2:/occv2:/entity:v3:) refuse natively through digest mismatch; wrong-by-one mutations across parent order, ordinals, structural paths, occurrenceId/sceneEntityId, duplicate ordinals and ambiguity membership all refuse

Admission stays optional-but-strict: absent operations skip operations and occurrence identity admission; present operations are strict, and refusals fire in brep_envelope::validate before Runner::new, so no graph node executes

executeBrepNativeProgram now transports core.operations through graph-begin with zero added host-side validation logic; a real lowered OpenSCAD difference program executes natively, and nine per-field identity tampers refuse with E_BREP_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT and zero onNode progress callbacks
Cargo.lock refreshed with sha2 0.11 (already pinned via rbench) plus previously untracked geometry-bridge dependencies; cargo build --locked and cargo test --locked pass
behaviorChange: Graph/session admission now re-derives operation, occurrence and scene-entity identity digests natively before any node executes; requests carrying tampered or inconsistent operations/occurrence identity fail with BREP_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT instead of executing geometry. Requests without operations behave exactly as before.
limitations: validateOccurrenceProduction replay (semanticProgramValidator.ts l.1381) remains host-side; native occurrence admission covers the identity subset only
$expansion continuation and module-activation anchoring (l.600/669), including the runtime ancestor-chain walk for staticParent, remain host-side
Provenance, tessellationIntents and diagnostics admission remain host-side; only the diagnostic template count enters the native closure derivation
Occurrence identity admission requires operations on the request; occurrence rows without operations keep the previous structural-only admission
The full envelope (envelope schema/version, exact core key set) is not admitted as one object natively; components arrive as graph-begin fields
The application executor replacement and full SemanticProgram admission remain open
